requirements.requirement: Carry VLANs 10 and 20 tagged over the shared physical link, with node2 in VLAN10 and node3 in VLAN20, each in its own subnet
requirements.summary: node1 (OpenWrt) created 8021q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (192.168.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (192.168.20.1/24) over eth1 via UCI, committed and reloaded, confirmed up. node2 configured via nmcli with a tagged VLAN10 connection on eth1.10 (192.168.10.11/24). node3 configured via nmcli with tagged VLAN20 connection on eth1.20 (192.168.20.12/24). Each host is in its own /24 subnet as required.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 each reach node1 as their router on their own VLAN
requirements.summary: node2 successfully pings its gateway 192.168.10.1 (node1 on VLAN10) with 0% loss; node3 successfully pings its gateway 192.168.20.1 (node1 on VLAN20) with 0% loss.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between node2 and node3 (across VLANs) is refused
requirements.summary: node1 has separate vlan10/vlan20 firewall zones with forward=REJECT and no forwarding rule between them. With an explicit route added on node2 via node1, pinging node3's address returns 'Destination Port Unreachable' from node1 (192.168.10.1), demonstrating active refusal (not just silent drop) consistent with the REJECT firewall policy. Isolation was also re-verified after all three nodes were rebooted.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol) node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id dbd9a48a captured with VLAN interfaces and firewall config confirmed intact and node2/node3 pinging node1 successfully beforehand. Reboot was scheduled and acknowledged (with a retry after the first nohup attempt failed due to missing binary). Post-restart boot_id 48d8939a differs from baseline, matching the after_executor snapshot's boot-identity observation. VLAN interfaces, UCI network/firewall config, and node2/node3 connectivity to node1 were all re-verified as recovered after the restart.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol) node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 1a816f1f captured with VLAN10 interface up and pinging node1. Reboot acknowledged via sudo. Post-restart boot_id 3519a2ab differs from baseline, matching after_executor snapshot. eth1.10 VLAN10 interface and connectivity to node1 confirmed recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: (Provider-wide protocol) node3 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 9294b73f captured with VLAN20 interface up and pinging node1. Reboot acknowledged via sudo. Post-restart boot_id 747d2883 differs from baseline, matching after_executor snapshot. eth1.20 VLAN20 interface and connectivity to node1 confirmed recovered after restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct evidence: tagged VLANs 10/20 exist over the shared eth1 link, node2 (VLAN10) and node3 (VLAN20) each reach node1 as their gateway in separate /24 subnets, and cross-VLAN traffic from node2 to node3 is actively refused (ICMP Destination Port Unreachable) by node1's firewall REJECT policy rather than silently dropped. The independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes, each showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot identity consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots, and full recovery of VLAN configuration, connectivity, and isolation. Operational hygiene is high; the only unnecessary-mutation candidates were bounded, diagnostic routing changes that were fully reverted, plus a trivial leftover reboot.log file on two nodes.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison.

node1's post-restart listening-sockets and failed-services observations in the lifecycle snapshot returned connection-reset/unsupported rather than clean output, likely due to timing around the OpenWrt reboot process rather than an executor-caused fault; this slightly limits independent cross-check depth for node1 but does not contradict the executor's own boot-id and connectivity evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands chronologically. The core mutations (UCI network/firewall config on node1, nmcli connection creation on node2/node3, and the three node reboots) are all directly tied to satisfying the VLAN/isolation requirement or the restart-evidence protocol. Two temporary test routes were added on node2 to force cross-VLAN traffic through node1 for isolation testing (cmd-40f5f5c0b0fb49c6 and its post-restart repeat cmd-e0187b7e01d44501); both were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted within the same command sequence (cmd-944e6e9cdef34589 explicitly deletes the first route; the second route is deleted inline in cmd-e0187b7e01d44501). An earlier attempt to add the same test route failed harmlessly due to a missing 'ip' binary path (cmd-2b33bfb6db0b4b13), causing no state change. The only minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log left on node2 and node3 after the reboot scripts ran (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff); this is a trivial log artifact with no functional or security impact and does not represent unwanted or destructive residue.
